report.summary: Two drift findings were identified (one action required and one review recommended); the highest-priority issue is the unmodeled, apparently unauthenticated bulk user export endpoint.

findings.title: Unauthenticated bulk user export endpoint is absent from the model

model_excerpt.quote: Login service exposing POST /login and GET /profile

evidence.note: The existing GET /profile route is explicitly wrapped with requireSession.
The new GET /admin/export route directly registers exportHandler without session or admin-authorization middleware.
The handler iterates over every user returned by the store.
Each user's ID, email, and creation time is written to the response.

relevance.justification: The change adds an unmodeled, apparently unauthenticated HTTP endpoint that bulk-exports user data, directly expanding the service's exposed attack surface.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl in threat_model "login service" to include the new GET /admin/export endpoint added at internal/httpapi/routes.go:10. Add a threat for unauthorized bulk user export and describe its current authentication/authorization state; do not mark an access-control control as implemented unless the endpoint is wrapped with appropriate middleware. The route is registered without requireSession while internal/httpapi/export.go:15-16 exports every user's ID, email, and creation time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add GET /admin/export and an unauthorized bulk-export threat to the login service model, with controls matching the endpoint's actual access checks.

findings.title: Exported email addresses and account metadata are unclassified

model_excerpt.quote: Usernames and password hashes in the users table

evidence.note: The new CSV schema contains id, email, and created_at fields.
The handler emits each user's email address and related account metadata.

relevance.justification: Email addresses and account metadata are personal data not covered by the narrowly defined user-credentials asset.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl by adding an information_asset block for user profile/export data, classified appropriately (for example Restricted), covering user IDs, email addresses, and account creation timestamps. The new CSV response declares these fields at internal/httpapi/export.go:14 and emits their values at line 16; the existing "user credentials" asset only covers usernames and password hashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a classified information asset for exported user profile data, including IDs, emails, and creation timestamps.
